cls: Serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor (SARI) antidepressant
pharm: Triazolopyridine antidepressant that inhibits serotonin reuptake and antagonizes 5-HT2A/2C, alpha-1-adrenergic and H1 receptors; the combined serotonergic modulation underlies antidepressant effect, while H1/alpha-1 blockade explains its sedation and orthostatic hypotension.
quick: Start 150 mg/day in divided doses; increase by 50 mg every 3-4 days; max 400 mg/day outpatient
Take shortly after a meal or light snack
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; limited data
Small amounts in milk; monitor infant for sedation/feeding
Use with caution; extensively hepatically metabolized
Avoid (additive CNS depression; overdose deaths reported)
Suicidality/clinical worsening, mood, BP, QT in at-risk patients
summary: Trazodone is a serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor (SARI) approved for major depressive disorder in adults. It carries the antidepressant class boxed warning for increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients. Sedation, orthostatic hypotension and rare priapism are characteristic; it is contraindicated with MAOIs and prolongs the QT interval.
indications: Not approved for use in pediatric patients

dosage.n: Give larger portion at bedtime if drowsy

dosage.d: Up to but not exceeding 600 mg/day in divided doses

admin: Take shortly after a meal or light snack to reduce dizziness/lightheadedness and increase absorption
Swallow whole or break in half along the score line; do not chew or crush
Give a larger portion of the daily dose at bedtime if drowsiness is a problem
Screen for bipolar disorder before starting
Taper gradually rather than stopping abruptly
Do not start within 14 days of an MAOI
moa: The antidepressant mechanism is not fully understood but relates to enhancement of central serotonergic activity. Trazodone inhibits neuronal reuptake of serotonin and is a potent antagonist at 5-HT2A receptors, with additional antagonism at 5-HT2B/2C, alpha-1 and alpha-2C adrenergic receptors and partial agonism at 5-HT1A. Alpha-1-adrenergic blockade contributes to postural hypotension, and antihistaminic activity to sedation.

absolute: Concomitant use of MAOIs, or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) - serotonin syndrome risk
relative: Known QT prolongation or use of other QT-prolonging drugs
History of priapism or predisposing conditions

preg: Limited human data. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; consider the risks of untreated maternal depression. Neonatal adaptation symptoms may occur with third-trimester exposure to serotonergic antidepressants.
lact: Trazodone is excreted in breast milk in small amounts. Weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against maternal need and monitor the infant for sedation and poor feeding.
renal: Limited data; use with caution in renal impairment and monitor for adverse effects.
hepatic: Trazodone is extensively metabolized by the liver (CYP3A4 to active metabolite mCPP); less than 1% is excreted unchanged. Use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: MAOIs including linezolid and IV methylene blue (contraindicated; serotonin syndrome)
Other serotonergic drugs - SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans, tramadol (serotonin syndrome)
QT-prolonging drugs and class IA/III antiarrhythmics (additive QT prolongation)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors - ritonavir, ketoconazole (increase trazodone levels; reduce dose)
moderate: CNS depressants and alcohol (additive sedation/respiratory depression)
Digoxin and phenytoin (may increase their serum levels)
interactions.food: Take shortly after food; food increases the amount absorbed and delays/reduces peak concentration.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; enhances CNS depression and overdose deaths have occurred with combined ingestion.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor PT/INR with warfarin; monitor ECG where QT risk exists.

emergency: Priapism lasting over a few hours (urologic emergency)

monitoring: Suicidal ideation and clinical worsening, especially early and after dose changes
Mood and screen for bipolar disorder
ECG/QT in patients with cardiac risk
counsel: Take shortly after a meal; drowsiness is common - take a larger share at bedtime if needed
Rise slowly from sitting or lying to avoid dizziness/fainting
Seek immediate care for a painful or prolonged erection (priapism)
Watch for new or worsening depression, agitation, or suicidal thoughts and report them
Do not stop abruptly; the dose should be tapered
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially other antidepressants and MAOIs
pk: Sleep effect within hours; antidepressant effect over 1-2 weeks or more
About 1 hour fasting; about 2 hours with food
Biphasic; terminal elimination approximately 5-9 hours (active metabolite mCPP longer)
pearls: Boxed warning: increased suicidal thoughts/behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients - monitor closely
Marked sedation (H1 and alpha-1 blockade) makes it widely used off-label for insomnia at low doses
Priapism is a characteristic emergency - counsel every male patient
Contraindicated with MAOIs; prolongs QT; avoid with other QT-prolonging drugs
Take after food and rise slowly to limit orthostatic hypotension
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, but if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. Bedtime doses missed may simply be skipped.
overdose: No specific antidote; consider multiple-drug involvement. Reported features include drowsiness, vomiting, priapism, respiratory arrest, seizures and QT prolongation; deaths have occurred with concurrent CNS depressants. Provide supportive care, cardiac monitoring, and contact a poison control center.
